en: Your party hunkers down in the old courthouse for the night. It has nothing in the way of comfortable furniture, but it's secure and has plenty of room, so it promises to be an easy night.

"The drums have been ensorcelled and are ready for use. Once they've been lit, this well should suffice as a..."
 *The note is ripped here, cutting off the rest of the journal page*

After the gruesome assault, you quickly return your attention to the well. Its surface shimmers softly, and you feel your gaze once again being drawn into it. Hopefully this will let you escape from this nightmare.
As the mayor speaks, he lurches forward, his body swelling and spilling forth from his dirty finery.
As you approach the well, the air grows taut, and a grating voice cuts through the oppressive silence.
As you enter the room, a sensation of nausea crashes over you like a wave.
As you near the edge of town, the path feels like it's getting longer and longer.
As you step outside, a dull vertigo tickles your mind.
The clear water of the well shimmers silently in the dark, reflecting the cloudy night sky.
The clear water of the well shimmers silently in the night, reflecting the cloudy sky and the flickering flames of the nearby fire drum.
The firelight reflecting in the water's surface is oddly alluring. Your gaze lingers for a moment, and a vague sense of nausea washes over you.
The stranger makes a sudden gesture, and you feel your vision growing dim, a furious howl echoing through the still darkness.
The water reflects a sickening sky with clouds like streaking blood on glass. You hope against hope that you can pass back through to the other side, but nothing seems to be happening.
Things appear to be back to normal for now, but there's no telling how long they will stay that way. You'd best escape this place while you can.
When you regain your composure, the room appears as if it has been remade in the image of a nightmare.
When your vision returns, the path is again clear. A foul odour lingers on the air, but there are no signs that anyone other than you has been here for many long years.
You are suddenly snapped back to your senses by a thumping noise in the building behind you. You are not alone here.
You eventually reach a crude stone barricade blocking your path, and when you turn to look, the town is still directly behind you. Some sinister force is holding you here.
You have stepped out of the nightmare, but there's no telling if it might drag you back in. You'd best leave while you can.
You may finally be able to escape.
It looks as though scavengers have already picked over the supplies. There is nothing useful remaining.
There is something glittering amid the broken body.
This corpse is partially eaten. Many of the bones are crushed or outright missing.
This corpse looks to have been savagely mangled by a large, powerful carnivore.
This corpse was cleanly torn in two
This person evidently got some distance away from the others before being felled.
This person never had a chance.
You find an amulet, once beautiful, but now crusted in dried blood.
It reads : The temple is reserved for those who can withstand the soul of the mountain.
Judging by the state of these corpses, these poor suckers fell down the mountainside. There are still some useful supplies among the bones.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Mountain Soul upon the pedestal?
There is an inscription on the dais here.
You decide to hold on to the Mountain Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Mountain Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
"Spartill Lodge."
"The Babe" is apparently quite far away, but it looks as though he and his band expected to get there quickly, based on the amount of supplies they prepared.
A large bathing room. The men who used this lodge must have been very comfortable with one another.

At the bottom, conspicuously, is written the phrase 
"Mother, mother, remember me."
Beauregard fishes a key out of his doublet and just holds it in front of his face for a few long minutes. This is clearly very hard for him.
Beauregard sighs deeply and hangs his head, looking at the ground.
It appears as if this room was used for cleaning and curing game. There are a number of hooks on chains hanging from the ceiling.
It seems to be a final farewell, as though he suspected that he would not be coming back.
Knowing that Spartill came here at the Queen's behest, you analyze the journal carefully.
On the inside wall of one of the shelves is a series of keyhooks, with a cold brass key still hanging, forgotten in the dark.
The beds are all neatly-made. It is unlikely that anyone has been here since the proper owner last left.
The final entry in this journal mentions "chasing the babe".
These appear to be accounts of hunting expeditions. Descriptions of where the men went, landmarks they observed, game they spotted, and of course, the chases and hunts themselves.
This calls to mind the image of a group of hunters enjoying their breakfast as they prepare for the day's activities.
This is penned in a straightforward hand with little flourish. Though some of the pages have faded and bled, it is all still quite legible.
This lodge has been undisturbed for a long time. There is a cozy sense of fellowship about it, despite the cobwebs.
You search through the groundskeeper's bookshelf.
He seems confused, and doesn't even notice you.
It looks as though the blacksmith clawed his way out of the grave.
Soon, your fingers grasp something solid, a long box. At its owner's direction, you open it and draw forth a magnificent sword.
The Mercenary Soul is drawn into the crystal, and it surges to life with a surprisingly violent flash.
The animated corpse makes no move to attack you. A voice like the sound of a blade being quenched hisses out when you get near.
The corpse stands by calmly and watches you as you gingerly begin to sift through the earth of his open grave.
The forge crystal sparkles with intense heat and light.
The piece is beautiful, precise, and elegant. The final work of a master smith whose name you never knew.
The skeletal face turns toward you. Though he has no eyes, you are certain he is looking straight at you.
The smith's body collapses into dust, and the only things left behind are his hammer and the piece he has forged for you.
This crystal is dull and appears covered in soot.
This crystal is dull and appears covered in soot. The mercenary soul throbs in your hand as you bring it near.
With one bony arm, he gestures toward the open earth behind him.
Without another word, the smith begins to work on your bezoar. You are unsure what he is making exactly, but he seemed to know precisely what you wanted, so you find a place to sit and let him work.
You gingerly hold out your bezoar, and the steelweaver's skeletal fingers curl around it carefully.

You take in the view of your surroundings from the top of this lookout tower. A short distance away is what appears to be a town in the forest below. It should be fairly easy to mark your direction and strike toward it.
The wall is sturdier than it first seemed. You'll need to try it again.
There is a forgotten scrap of bread in this box.
This wall appears to be barely holding. You might be able to break through it.
Whatever was in this cauldron is now nothing but a foul-smelling slime.
A woman in a dull robe is praying before the altar of this abbey, her lips moving in silent homage. After a moment, she straightens and turns toward you.
Borgnina appears to be uneasy.
Borgnina is silent for a moment. She takes a deep sigh and looks down at her hands, clad in heavy jointed armour.
Borgnina withdraws a handful of unassuming jewels from her robe and hands them to you.
It appears to be positioned in the northwest corner of the abbey, so it would make a good place for one of the jewels.
It appears to be the northeast corner of the abbey, so you drop one of the jewels into the bin.
It looks as though the nuns have set up a place to watch songbirds playing in the water. It's a lovely, quiet place.
It looks as though this box is full of various soaps and personal care items. They smell quite pleasant, but they must be hard to get out here. The sisters probably make them.
She shouts aloud, "Sisters! In the name of God, we shall purge this evil from our world! Come!"
Some of these items are clearly luxuries, and not strictly necessary for hygeine.
Suddenly she whirls around toward you, brandishing her mace menacingly.
The table is in the southwest corner of the abbey though, so it makes a good spot to plant one of the crystals.
There are ashes from a burnt-out stick of incense sitting here.

These barrels have preserved meats alongside some other long-storage foodstuffs. Anyone can tell you that storing those foods in the same barrel is against religious practices, but it technically doesn't harm anything.
This book is certainly unbecoming of a nun, but it's not exactly demonic.
This might once have been a hallway or another room, but it has long since collapsed.
This spot appears to lay beneath the southeast corner of the abbey, however. You drop one of the jewels into the open chest.
This stone chest lies empty.
This table is laid out with some pieces for a simple dice game. The player with the red pieces is clearly winning. This kind of game is not very nun-like.
This wastebin is full of discarded vegetable peels. Perhaps they save them for something?
A clutch of harpies springs out from their roost in the cliffs, and before anyone can react, they have completely surrounded Bato.
As quickly as you can, you send for help from your stronghold.
Far below, you can see the waves crashing against the base of the cliff in an angry froth.
It is probably better that you don't.
It takes a few hours, but working together, you eventually manage to get the two of them back up to the top of the cliff.
One of the harpies latches onto Bato and pulls him, flailing and screaming over the edge of the cliff!
The initials "N G" are written.
The initials "T W" are written.
The thought of jumping occurs to you suddenly, almost desperately.
Beauregard and Grant appear to be getting along today better than usual. You decide not to draw attention to it so as not to spoil the peaceful moment.
Beauregard takes a deep draught of the warm night air and turns his gaze to the sky.
In the morning, you awaken to a mouth-watering smell, as heavy slabs of fresh venison roast over a pit of open coals.
This weather-worn satchel is almost impossible to see amid the greenery. You find a dirty bundle of coins inside.
With a hearty breakfast in your belly and a bright morning sun lighting the way, you're able to get back to the path with little difficulty.
Your party settles into the old shack for the night, and you quickly succumb to the embrace of your bedroll.
A voice like a shrill hiss calls out, "Turn back!"
As if in warning, a darkness descends over you, snuffing out your torch.
It reads : The Jackals know.
Someone has scrawled something on the base of this statue in a shaky hand.
The darkness of the tomb coalesces into a savage form and attacks you!
An old chest, sealed tight with weather and age.
It feels a bit petty, but you scrape up a handful of coins from the well. They're perfectly workable.
It is difficult to get a decent grip on the lid to force it. Perhaps another attempt will open it.
It looks as though someone carrying a lot of goods was attacked and left for dead here. Most of the rubble has been picked-over, but there is one heavily-damaged chest that is still sealed.
It looks as though someone made a hasty attempt to hide this satchel. It has a few items inside.
It takes a bit of creative leverage, but you manage to pop the lid off of the sealed chest.
It's just full of stagnant rainwater, filmed over with scum and wriggling bug larvae.
The lock is old and quite seized. This may take another attempt.
There are coins glittering in the bottom of the well.
This well is overflowing with cool, clear water. It appears to be built on some kind of natural spring.
With a mighty heave, the lid gives way and slides onto the ground.
Would you like to throw some coins into the well?
You throw a handful of coins into the clear water and watch as they tumble to the bottom, glittering on the way down. For a moment, there is a comfortable feeling. Maybe you'll get lucky!
A moment later you are jarred awake as you are slammed into a rocky outcropping. You drag yourself out of the water, but you are a long distance from where you started.
A warm breeze blows through the inlet, and the empty mantis husks dissolve into dust, drifting on the wind.
From here, you can see that there is an inlet with something peculiar at its end. It looks like the current would carry you directly into it if you let it.
It is a difficult swim, but you manage to push through it and climb onto the opposite bank.
It looks like there used to be a pier on the opposite bank, but the river has since washed it away. There would be no way for you to climb out of the water if you swam over.
It takes everything you've got, but you manage to keep apace and make it to the opposite shore.
Not until the party has been reunited.
Not until the party is reuinted.

One of these papers has a drawing of the layout of this area on it. Apparently someone was planning on rebuilding the bridges, but the paper is so old and worn that you doubt whoever drew this is going to return.
Swimming across one by one is too risky. There must be a way to make crossing easier.
The current is stronger than you expect. You're dashed against the rocks and manage to climb to shore a short distance downstream.
The current is stronger than you expect. You're dashed against the rocks, but manage to climb to shore a short distance downstream.
The powerful current drags you under, and you are swept away.
The water looks rough, but if you swim across, you might be able to find a way to help the others follow.
The wind has moved on, and the inlet is once again still and quiet.
There are dead mantis husks clinging to this statue. For whatever reason, they haven't been picked off by birds or other predators.
There is nothing in the sack but a few stones. Apparently it was set here as bait for an ambush.
These barrels don't have anything in them, but they still seem to be watertight. They would probably float.
This gap is much wider than the others. It's going to take a very strong swimmer to make it across.
Though it's hardly easy, the barrels lodged in the rocks make crossing the river on foot doable. It takes a few minutes, but you get everybody safely across.
Using the lodged barrels as footholds, you're able to cross the water with relative ease.
Would you like to cross to the opposite bank?
You are dashed against the rocks and thrown onto a bank a short distance downstream. Your party makes their way back to you and pulls you out of the muck.
You are reminded of the chunk of slag you are carrying. Make an offering of the Mantis Soul?
You could jump into the water from here and try to swim to the opposite pier, but the rock you are standing on is far too high to climb back onto.
You let the current carry you into the inlet, and climb onto a low rock.
You push the empty barrels into the water, and they float downstream.
You swim to the pier, and your party makes it back in time to help you out of the water.
"I think I just juiced in my shorts a little. Would you say "treasure" a few more times for me, Captain? A little deeper and slower, please."
Bato sneers up at Rangda and puffs out his chest.
Inside is a magnificent sword, clearly meant for someone of much importance. It seems that Captain Arris' sword is now yours.
It looks as though this machine has been torn apart for salvage.
It looks as though this manacannon is still functional. If you loaded a cannonball into the barrel, you could fire it.
Looks like that one shot was all you get.
Someone has made an attempt to hide something by covering it with an old sack.
The chain on this winch stretches down into the depths, and the handle gives firm resistance. It appears to be attached to something.
The handle and the footing beneath are both slippery. Perhaps another attempt would fare better.
The manacannon is loaded and ready to fire. Do you want to fire it?
There are still a few items left inside this discarded satchel.
There is a cannonball inside one of these barrels.
There is nothing of interest inside the barrels.
This chest is secured with a custom lock. You'll need to get the proper key.
This console does not appear to be functional.
This is a manacannon barrel, but it appears to be broken.
This manacannon is loaded and ready to fire.
This manacannon looks functional, but it is not loaded. If you had a cannonball, you could load it here.
This node appears to still have some power left in it.
Would you like to load the manacannon?
You are able to levitate a cannonball out of one of the barrels.
You load your cannonball into the barrel.
You use the key you found on Captain Arris, and the lock pops open with ease.
You wind the chain up, and there is a heavy wooden chest hooked to the other end!

As his story draws to a close, he turns his face back to the sea, and you catch a glimpse of a brand on his neck. 
"Traitor"
As his story draws to a close, he turns his face back to the sea, and you catch a glimpse of a brand on his neck.
Logus goes on at length with a tale of a seafaring adventure. It is obvious from his story that he is an experienced sailor, and he speaks with great fondness and longing.
Logus scratches his beard thoughtfully, the edge of a grin beginning to form.
Logus stands up and takes a deep breath of sea air before pulling his hat low over his eyes and flashing you a scoundrel's grin.
Logus turns toward you with intense eyes. He runs his tongue against one of his tusks as he sizes you up before finally speaking.
Sitting here, staring out over the grey sea is a weathered old orc, dressed in the tatters of a sea captain's uniform. As you approach, he glances up toward you.
The herbalist mixes a potion for you.
There is a sturdy length of rope tied to this mooring. The sailor's knot is easily undone, and you are able to coil up a decent amount of rope.
This chest is fastened securely with a unique lock. You'll need the key.
And so, you can remain civil even in the face of that which must surely shock you? Intriguing.
And you are so bold as to say it before me, even knowing nothing of my power?
But no matter. The test to prove your worth is long past, and your reward is nigh. Behold!
I give you the bow that wounded the sun.
Now, stay and avail yourself of my hospitality for as long as it pleases you.
Tell me, hero. Does the sight of my court disgust you?
The water whispered to me of your coming. This island has long been a place of madness, but you come to impose your order.
This table is laid out with a mouthwatering display.
Welcome. Avail yourself of my food and drink if it pleases you.
You decide against it.
A patch of plump mushrooms sprouts here. This variety is known to be edible, if foul-tasting.
Inside the mouldering barrel, you find a torch that seems dry enough to use.
This chest has been weakened by years of moisture and neglect. You find a handful of coins inside.
This chest smells strongly of wine. Although most of it has broken and soaked into the wood, you find an unopened phial in the corner.
This signboard has the layout for the tunnel scrawled on it.
"I can't believe I scored the Breakfast suite! This is gonna be great! They send someone to wake you up in the morning, and you know what that means!"
"I don't think I would classify those looks I am getting as "overcome with animal desire", would you? I can't even remember the last time I dug a rut."
"I guess I'll just keep my fingers crossed. Odds are I'll get one of the ladies anyway, right?"
"I heard that they "share product" with the Ettins in order to get them to stand guard like that. Which unlucky girl do you think gets that job?"
"It would probably be weird having someone without any tusks doing that anyway, wouldn't it? Ugh, why am I stuck between toothless human girls or orcs with beards?"
"Of course, now I'm not going to be able to sleep. At least they have lots of books."
"What am I gonna do if he's the "room service"?"
After a loud and satisfying half-hour, Leftie wipes himself off with a wadded-up bedsheet and stands up.
At first he seems like he is going to argue, but then his voice pours out of him with an audible note of relief.
By the sounds of things, she's currently busy.
Give your spool of wire to Braisa?
He is ample and forceful enough to be exciting, even if his technique is somewhat basic.
He laughs, apparently thinking that your compliment was sarcastic.
He takes notice of you sizing him up and sighs heavily.
It is clear that he has little if any experience being intimate with other men, but he doesn't back down, and takes his cues from you attentively.
It sounds like an intimate moment. You'd best leave them to it.
Leftie is not a graceful lover, but he eagerly does what is expected, and follows through on your deal.
Leftie takes in a deep breath, and a dour smile creeps across his lips.
Logus' face flushes, and he abruptly stops with his inquiry.
Mailee slowly disrobes and then removes your clothes as well.
Mailee's hands are velvet soft, and she guides her fingers over your body with practiced ease.
Rugal is not courteous, but he is powerful, ferocious, and relentless.
Rugal wastes no time with pleasantries and gets straight to business.
Shapiro laughs.
That sounds like a private conversation.
The gigantic man sounds mechanical, his line rehearsed. Though he clearly has the stature to be intimidating, he is not making any effort.
The two-headed giant is watching you closely, evidently acting as a guard.
This room appears to belong to a Ms. Zianne.
